title: The supplied cone equation for the third morphism of a distinguished completion.
statement: For a triangulated functor F and a saturated triangulated multiplicative system S, let T be a distinguished triangle and let LX, LY, LZ be its left-derived values. Supply value cones uX, uY, uZ with their retraction and common-stage conditions, and maps lf and lg satisfying all denominator-square equations for T.mor₁ and T.mor₂. There exists lh : LZ → LX[1] such that (LX, LY, LZ, lf, lg, lh) is distinguished and uZ(s) F(h′) = lh [1](uX(s′)) commShiftIso(F,1)⁻¹ whenever s T.mor₃ = h′ [1](s′). This asserts existence of a compatible completion, not compatibility of an arbitrary distinguished completion.

proof.text: Complete lf by TR1 to the distinguished triangle (LX,LY,K,lf,b,c). Keep a supplied retracting denominator sY with beta. MS2 gives a square lifting T.mor1 to sY at a denominator s1. Apply the common-stage clause of uX to s1, obtaining a:s -> sX and t:s -> s1 with F(t)=F(a) alpha0 uX(s1). Define alpha=F(a) alpha0 and fprime=t followed by the lift. Naturality and uX(sX) alpha0=id give uX(s) alpha=id. The factorization equation, hf at s1 and beta retraction give F(fprime) beta=alpha lf. This construction does not need to equalize arrows or impose S-membership on a or t.

Complete fprime to a distinguished triangle U by TR1. Apply MS6 to the two denominator components to get p:U -> T with all three components in S. Apply F to U and use TR3 with alpha,beta and their first-square equation to get q:F(U) -> (LX,LY,K). Keep its second and third squares and both first-vertex and second-vertex retraction identities.

Apply [lem-pur-triangle-retraction-hom-colimit] to U,p,q and the supplied cones at LX,LY. This gives, for every W, the bijection Hom(K,W) -> colim Hom(F(Zprime),W), represented by gamma=q.hom3 at sK=p.hom3. Apply [lem-pur-essential-constant-pro-criterion-05py] to obtain a cone uK with uK(sK) gamma=id and its identity-class equations. For each j, equality of these representatives in the filtered type colimit is witnessed at a common stage k. The resulting equality F(b)=F(a) gamma uK(j) supplies the common-stage certificate for this very cone.

Use [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] for T.mor2 from LY to the newly constructed value K, obtaining lb and all its denominator-square equations. At the concrete p2,p3 square, compose its equation with gamma. The equation uK(sK) gamma=id and the retained second square F(U.mor2) gamma=beta b imply lb=uY(p2) beta b=b. Thus b has every denominator-square equation for T.mor2.

Use [lem-pur-derived-functor-shift-05su] to get a value V at T.obj1[1] and a canonical isomorphism eV:LX[1] -> V preserving the shifted legs of uX. Retraction and common-stage certificates make uX and the extracted V cone limits: for another cone v take v(j0) r; common-stage factorization proves each leg equation and u(j0) r=id proves uniqueness. Apply [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] to T.mor3:K -> V and put lc=lc0 eV.inv. For every hprime square, its shifted target denominator lies in S by MS5. The morphism equation followed by eV.inv, and the leg equation for eV, give uK(s) F(hprime)=lc shift(uX(sprime)) commShiftIso.inv. At the concrete p3,shift(p1) square compose with commShiftIso.hom and shift(alpha). The right side is lc since shift(uX(p1) alpha)=id. The third square of q makes the left side uK(sK) gamma c=c. Hence lc=c, establishing the third equation for c without asserting it for an arbitrary completion lacking the retained comparison.

The direct cone-limit argument above makes uK and the supplied uZ limits of the same denominator diagram. Let e:K -> LZ be their unique cone-point isomorphism, so e.hom uZ(s)=uK(s) for every s. MS2 gives a denominator square for T.mor2 with the retracting target leg sZ of uZ. The b cone equation and hg imply (b e.hom) uZ(sZ)=lg uZ(sZ); composing with its right inverse gives b e.hom=lg. Put lh=e.inv c. Triangle.isoMk with identities on LX,LY and e on K transports distinguishedness. Compose the c cone equation with e.inv, using e.inv uK(s)=uZ(s), to obtain the required universal shifted cone equation.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05SC, LF dual; retraction Hom-colimit comparison 05SC, pro criterion 05PY, morphisms 05SA, shift 05SU. Common-stage construction and supplied-cone comparison made explicit by C1.

theorem leftDerived_value_triangle_extension_compat
    {C : Type u} {D : Type uD} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{vD} D]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C]
    [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (S : MorphismProperty C)
    (hS : S.IsSaturatedTriangulatedMultiplicativeSystem)
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (LX LY LZ : D)
    (hX : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₁ LX)
    (hY : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₂ LY)
    (hZ : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₃ LZ)
    (uX : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁)).obj LX ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₁ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₁ ⋙ F)
    (uY : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂)).obj LY ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₂ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₂ ⋙ F)
    (uZ : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃)).obj LZ ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₃ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₃ ⋙ F)
    (huX : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LX,
      uX.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LX ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uX.app s)
    (huY : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LY,
      uY.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LY ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uY.app s)
    (huZ : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LZ,
      uZ.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LZ ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uZ.app s)
    (lf : LX ⟶ LY) (lg : LY ⟶ LZ)
    (hf : ∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂)
        (f' : s.left ⟶ s'.left),
        s.hom ≫ T.mor₁ = f' ≫ s'.hom →
          uX.app s ≫ F.map f' = lf ≫ uY.app s')
    (hg : ∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃)
        (g' : s.left ⟶ s'.left),
        s.hom ≫ T.mor₂ = g' ≫ s'.hom →
          uY.app s ≫ F.map g' = lg ≫ uZ.app s')
    : ∃ lh : LZ ⟶ (shiftFunctor D (1 : ℤ)).obj LX,
        Triangle.mk lf lg lh ∈ distTriang D ∧
        (∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁)
          (h' : s.left ⟶ (shiftFunctor C (1 : ℤ)).obj s'.left),
          s.hom ≫ T.mor₃ = h' ≫ (shiftFunctor C (1 : ℤ)).map s'.hom →
            uZ.app s ≫ F.map h' =
              lh ≫ (shiftFunctor D (1 : ℤ)).map (uX.app s') ≫
                (F.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).inv.app s'.left)

statement_change.old_statement: The supplied cone equation for the third morphism of a distinguished completion.
statement_change.what: The old Lean signature universally asserted cone compatibility for an arbitrary distinguished completion. The split triangle X → 0 → X[1] with third map ±identity refutes that implication. The corrected existential conclusion retains both distinguishedness and compatibility; it remains unproved and closes no hole.

old_proof.text: This intermediate statement isolates one strictly smaller part of the construction in Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Lemma 05SC; its proof is the corresponding construction using the listed denominator, triangulated, shift, and essential-constancy results.
